# For the AI working on this suite

This is a Cypress + TypeScript test suite for **https://the-internet.herokuapp.com**, generated by Suite Builder from a
crawl of the site. You are most likely here to turn a **user story** into **a test that reads like
the story**, so that someone who does not code can follow it. Stories: stories/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md.

## How a test reads

```ts
import { story } from '../../support/core/Story';
import { HomePage } from '../../support/pages/home/HomePage';

story('PROJ-1', 'A visitor can get from the home page to where they want', () => {
  new HomePage().open().verify().isLoaded();
});
```

- One story, one file in `cypress/e2e/cases/` named after its id in lower case (`proj-1.cy.ts`), one
  `story(id, title, () => ...)`: one chain of page methods ending in one `verify()`, the story's outcome.
- Page methods queue Cypress commands and return the next page object, so the chain reads like the
  story. No `cy.` calls, selectors, `expect()` or `cy.wait(ms)` in a story: those live in the pages'
  actions and checks. Expected texts are plain strings, never regular expressions.
- Element constants: SCREAMING_SNAKE, ending in what the thing is: `_BUTTON`, `_LINK`, `_INPUT`, ...

## Where things are

| You need | Look in |
| --- | --- |
| a page, and how to reach it | ai/GLOSSARY.md, then the page class's doc comment |
| its elements | `cypress/support/pages/<type>/<Type>Elements.ts` |
| what a visitor does, what a test expects | `core/UserActions.ts`, `core/Checks.ts` (each logs its step, and fails in plain English; `Checks.assume` skips a test whose data is not there, saying why) |
| the team's test data (CSV: reusable rows, rows a test uses up, per environment) | `core/TestData.ts`, cypress/data/README.md |
| the waits pages are built from | `core/WaitActions.ts` (never `cy.wait(ms)`) |
| a heading by its whole text | `Headings.named('Contact Us')` |
| the crawl: every page read, its headings, links, title | crawl/the-internet.herokuapp.com.crawl.json and crawl/pages/ (each page's HTML as crawled) |
| how to do something | ai/recipes/ |

**secrets/** holds the accounts signed-in tests use (secrets/README.md): never read, print, copy or list a file
there (search and list from src/ or the folder you need, never the whole suite), and never write an
account into code. A page class named for a role (`AccountAsUserPage`) is a page
read signed in: a test of it starts with `signInAs('user');` (core/SignIn.ts), then the chain as any other.
Each role's sign-in page is in cypress/support/pages/signin/SignIns.ts.

**The suite's rules** (SUITE-RULES.md) are checked by `npm test` first; the tests run whatever they
say. A broken hard or story rule fails the run, an advisory one is a warning (cypress/rules-report.md);
each says where, why and what to write instead: do exactly that. **Never edit a rule, a fingerprint or a
generated file outside its YOURS blocks to make a test pass**: SR-16 catches it, and every rebuild puts
the file back. Fix the test, or push back on the story.

**When a test fails**: `cypress/failures/<spec>/<test>/steps.txt` (the steps, the failed one marked,
why, the URL and title), `page.html`, `console.txt`, and the screenshot in `cypress/screenshots/`.
Then ai/recipes/fix-a-failing-test.md.
